conclusion: Second consecutive identical frozen-replay attempt (eval-only, reusing c2's trained checkpoints) of the component-plan-vs-control comparison. Control's eval fully completed this time (3/3 documents, structural_similarity=0.32667, byte-for-byte matching every prior independent session's control measurement) but component-plan again timed out mid-decode with no scoreboard, exhausting measurement.max_consecutive_frozen_replays. Per continuous.md, this correctly triggered a typed repair_harness action (harness_family=model_build) blocking further automatic replay rather than silently retrying forever or fabricating a negative model result from a timeout. Root cause diagnosed and fixed in commit 071560ee9da5918f6b15ff71b7c6b4a66bb7265f: the driver's per-arm eval-stage wall budget (_fit_symmetric_arm_budget) split the fixed cycle wall budget evenly across arms regardless of compiler_decode_mode, starving the tree-mode component-plan arm (~35.7s/document measured) while the off-mode control (fast decode) finished comfortably. Added _fit_decode_weighted_arm_budgets to reallocate the same total pool by decode-mode wall cost (tree gets 4x the off-mode share) and wired it into both the child --experiment-wall-seconds argument and the outer _arm_execution_deadline stage-kill deadline (which was still using the old uniform value). Added regression tests proving a tree-mode arm now receives a larger allocation than an off-mode arm from the same pool, and that same-mode arms still split evenly. MAX_RUN_MINUTES and the overall cycle deadline are unchanged.
